speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work confirms severe anemia and thrombocytopenia, and the bone marrow showing immature cells positive for CD10, CD19, and TdT is highly characteristic of lymphoblastic leukemia. Given the fever and bone pain, I need to rule out complications like osteomyelitis or spinal cord compression. Please tell me if you have noticed any back pain, numbness in your legs, or difficulty walking. REQUEST IMAGES: X-ray of the femur and pelvis.

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing generalized fatigue and easy bruising for 3 weeks. Over the past week, she has developed a fever and severe leg pain that wakes her up at night.

speaker: Doctor
text: The bone marrow findings of CD10, CD19, and TdT positive cells strongly confirm acute lymphoblastic leukemia. While the leg pain is likely due to marrow expansion, I must rule out spinal cord compression before starting treatment. Please tell me if she has any numbness, tingling, or weakness in her legs, and if she has complained of back pain. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
